chunk_findings.detail: The test is vacuous: it can never fail, on this change or on current main, so it does not guard the scenario the intent assigns to it ("a removed item in the clone that removed it (which already disposes the tree) ... do not produce the PROBLEM"). Walk `_two_clones(tmp_path, alice_claims=True)`: clone `b` is created with `_clone(remote, ...)` at line 60, i.e. **before** alice runs `claim T2` at line 62, and alice's claim event is only committed locally (`_commit_log(a, "alice log")`, line 71) and never pushed — the only `push` to `origin` is bob's, at line 68, and `b` never pulls it. Consequently bob's clone's event log contains no `claim`/lease event for T2 at all, so the fold in `stranded_leases` cannot see a live holder and `doctor` cannot emit the PROBLEM regardless of whether the new detection logic is correct, broken, or over-eager. To actually exercise requirement 5 the lease must be visible in `b` (alice must push her claim commit and `b` must pull it) while `b` is the clone that removed the item and has already disposed of the T2 worktree; as written the assertion `"ddflow release T2" not in out + err` is satisfied by an empty/silent doctor and by every plausible regression of the fix.

chunk_findings.detail: The new branch fires on `it.lease` / `gone.lease` being truthy rather than on the lease being *live*. Leases here are deadline-based (heartbeat already imports `localize` from `services.leaseclock` to render lease deadlines, and the existing cleanup path already distinguishes "LEAVE ALONE (live lease)"), so a removed item can still carry a lease record whose deadline has passed without anyone having released it. For such an item `_require` now returns `O.refused` with the stranded text ("item removed, lease still held by <holder>: release it, then keep or delete the branch") and `heartbeat` refuses with exit 3, even though no holder holds anything. Demonstration: take an item that is removed while a lease record with a past deadline remains in state (lease expired, never released) and run `ddflow merge T2` / `ddflow complete T2` / `ddflow heartbeat T2` — each now emits the lease-held remedy and exit 3 instead of the plain removal message, while `doctor`/`cleanup` (which check liveness) correctly treat the lease as dead and stay silent. The prescribed remedy `ddflow release T2` is itself a no-op on a dead lease, so the user is steered to a command that cannot clear the condition. Requirement (5) and the design ("a lease is evidence of intent", "an item removed with NO live lease … do not produce the PROBLEM") scope this behavior to live leases; both guards should use the same liveness predicate that cleanup uses, e.g. only report/hold off when the lease is still within its deadline.

chunk_findings.detail: `stranded_leases` treats an item as stranded in *this* clone if the branch exists **or** the worktree path exists, so the clone that removed the item will still report the lease whenever that clone happens to hold the removed item's branch. This contradicts requirement (5) and the stated design ("removal does not destroy a holder's branch"), whose only stated reason for the removing clone being safe is that it "already disposes the tree" — i.e. only the worktree check distinguishes the removing clone. Concrete input: clone B has previously claimed T2 (so `refs/heads/ddflow/T2` exists locally as a stale branch), it loses the lease to clone A, and then runs `ddflow remove T2` while A's lease on T2 is still live. Removal disposes B's worktree but leaves the branch (the design explicitly does not destroy the holder's branch), so `W.branch_exists(root, "ddflow/T2")` is True in B even though `W.load_path(root, it.worktree)` no longer exists. `stranded_leases` therefore returns T2 for clone B, `doctor` exits 1 with the PROBLEM in the very clone that removed the item, and `cleanup` relabels the branch `stranded` (printed as a problem) instead of leaving the removing clone silent — exactly the case requirement (5) says must produce nothing. With the OR reduced to the worktree/tree check (or otherwise requiring this clone to actually hold the holder's work), the removing clone stays silent while the holder's clone — where the worktree or branch genuinely is — still reports.

chunk_findings.detail: `_require` decides whether a removed item's lease counts as live using `_GRACE`, a module-level value computed once at import from a bare `Config()` (the shipped/default config), while `heartbeat()` uses the repo's loaded `cfg.lease.grace_s` (heartbeat.py:38). `merge`/`complete` are not in the changed file set, so they necessarily call `_require(st, item, kind)` without the new `grace_s` argument and therefore always take the default. Result: in any repo that overrides `[lease] grace_s` (the value is plainly configurable — that is why heartbeat reads it from `cfg`), the two paths disagree for any lease whose age falls between the shipped default and the configured value. Concretely, with a repo setting `grace_s` larger than the shipped default and an item removed by bob whose holder alice last renewed long enough ago to be lapsed under the default but still live under the repo setting, alice's pull yields: `heartbeat T2` → the required removal/branch refusal (exit 3), but `merge T2` / `complete T2` → `_require` computes `live(..., _GRACE)` as false and returns the old `O.failed(kind, "no such item 'T2' (it was removed from the queue)")` (exit 1). That is exactly the "bare 'no such item'" behaviour requirement (3) of this change forbids, and the regression test does not catch it because it runs on the default config. The comment justifying the default ("callers that hold no config") is false for these callers: they run `_load(repo, agent)` and already have `cfg`, so `cfg.lease.grace_s` should be passed through (or the whole check moved onto the loaded config) rather than a frozen import-time default.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/_common.py:12–27 (`_GRACE` / `_require`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_require` judges liveness with `_GRACE = Config().lease.grace_s` (the shipped default, resolved at import time), while `heartbeat()` and `stranded_leases`/doctor judge it with `cfg.lease.grace_s` from `_load(repo, agent)`. These two thresholds only coincide when the repo leaves `[lease].grace_s` at the shipped value; the fact that `heartbeat` reads the configured value shows it is meant to be overridable. Concrete failure: a repo with `[lease].grace_s = 900` (shipped default, say, 120) where the holder's lease deadline lapsed 10 minutes ago on an item that was just removed. `heartbeat T2` (heartbeat.py:34, `gone.lease.live(time.time(), cfg.lease.grace_s)`) correctly refuses with the removal/holder/branch/remedy text, and `doctor` agrees — but `merge T2` / `complete T2` now fall through the new branch (`it.lease.live(time.time(), _GRACE)` is false) and return `O.failed("no such item T2 (it was removed from the queue)")`, i.e. exactly the bare "no such item" that requirement (3) of this fix says they must no longer emit, leaving the branch unreachable from those commands again. The comment claims the callers "hold no config", but they must already have `st` from `_load(repo, agent)` (which also returns `cfg`), so the repo's `cfg.lease.grace_s` is available and should be threaded through the new `grace_s` parameter; using a value captured from `Config()` at import time additionally ties the threshold to whatever config was current when the module was first imported rather than to the state's repo.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/_common.py:11 (`_GRACE` / `_require`'s liveness check)

chunk_findings.detail: `stranded_leases` deliberately defines "stranded in this clone" as *lease live and mine* AND (`branch_exists(branch)` OR `load_path(worktree).exists()`), so an item whose branch is here but whose worktree is not is still stranded — and `doctor` (via the same helper) will report a PROBLEM for it. But in `cleanup()` the resulting map is consulted in exactly one place, the *worktree* loop (`elif protected == "held" and branch in stranded`, feeding `t.kind = "stranded"`); the branch-only pass (the code that owns `by_branch`/`by_path`/`seen_branches`, which the `seen_branches` set exists to keep from re-processing branches already covered by a worktree) was not taught about `stranded`. Input: alice's clone holds a live lease on T2, has her commit on `ddflow/T2`, but the T2 worktree is gone (pruned, or disposed after an earlier merge) — bob removes T2 and alice pulls. `doctor` now flags the removed item with the holder/branch, yet `cleanup` in that same clone still prints `LEAVE ALONE (live lease)` for `ddflow/T2`, because the worktree loop never visits the branch and no other site looks at `stranded`. That is precisely the outcome requirement (4) forbids ("cleanup lists the branch (not 'LEAVE ALONE') as 'item removed, lease still held by <holder>…'"), so for branch-backed-but-worktree-less strands the fix leaves the B71dedb76d2 symptom intact while the two commands disagree.
